system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}
user:
CONCEPT: He-Schramm theorem
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: In scope: the CP parabolic / CP hyperbolic dichotomy for one-ended triangulations, the equivalence with recurrence/transience under bounded degree, the roles of the bounded-degree assumption in each part, the counterexample with unbounded degrees, and uniqueness of the packings. Excluded: the detailed technical proof of the existence parts.

ATOMS:
- MATH-PROB-C08-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: Every one-ended infinite triangulation can be circle packed so that the carrier is either the plane or the open unit disk, but not both.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-PROB-p0015-s03] Theorem 1.6 (He and Schramm 1993) Any one-ended infinite triangulation can be circle packed such that the carrier is either the plane or the open unit disk, but not both.
- MATH-PROB-C08-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: For a one-ended infinite triangulation with bounded degrees, the triangulation is CP parabolic if and only if it is recurrent for simple random walk, that is, if and only if the simple random walk on it visits every vertex infinitely often almost surely.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-PROB-p0019-s05] Theorem 1.10 (He and Schramm 1995) Let T be a one-ended infinite triangulation.
    [MATH-PROB-p0019-s06] If T has bounded degrees, then it is CP parabolic if and only if it is recurrent for simple random walk, that is, if and only if the simple random walk on T visits every vertex infinitely often almost surely.
- MATH-PROB-C08-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: An infinite one-ended simple planar triangulation is called CP parabolic if it can be circle packed in $\mathbb{C}$, and CP hyperbolic if it can be circle packed in the open unit disk $\mathbb{U}$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-PROB-p0015-s08] In view of Theorem 1.6, we call an infinite one-ended simple planar triangulation CP parabolic if it can be circle packed in C, and call it CP hyperbolic if it can be circle packed in the open unit disk U.
- MATH-PROB-C08-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: For a one-ended infinite planar triangulation, if it is CP parabolic then its circle packing in $\mathbb{C}$ is unique up to dilations, rotations, translations and reflections, and if it is CP hyperbolic then its circle packing in $\mathbb{U}$ is unique up to Möbius transformations or reflections fixing $\mathbb{U}$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-PROB-p0016-s01] Theorem 1.8 (Schramm 1991) Let T be a one-ended infinite planar triangulation.
    [MATH-PROB-p0016-s02] • If T is CP parabolic, then its circle packing in C is unique up to dilations, rotations, translations and reflections. • If T is CP hyperbolic, then its circle packing in U is unique up to Möbius transformations or reflections fixing U.
- MATH-PROB-C08-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: For an infinite simple plane triangulation $G$ with bounded degrees, if $G$ is recurrent then there exists a circle packing of $G$ with carrier $\mathbb{R}^2$, and if $G$ is transient then there exists a circle packing of $G$ with carrier $\mathbb{U}$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-PROB-p0060-s11] Theorem 4.4 (He and Schramm [40]) Let G be an infinite simple plane triangulation with bounded degrees.
    [MATH-PROB-p0060-s12] 1. If G is recurrent, then there exists a circle packing P of G such that Carrier(P) = R2. 2.
    [MATH-PROB-p0060-s13] If G is transient, then there exists a circle packing P of G such that Carrier(P) = U.
- MATH-PROB-C08-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: If $T$ is a CP hyperbolic infinite one-ended simple planar triangulation and $D \subsetneq \mathbb{C}$ is a simply connected domain, then there exists a circle packing of $T$ with carrier $D$, so a circle packing of a CP hyperbolic triangulation is in general not determined up to Möbius transformations and reflections.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-PROB-p0015-s09] Theorem 1.7 (He and Schramm 1995) Let T be a CP hyperbolic infinite oneended simple planar triangulation and let D ⊊C be a simply connected domain.
    [MATH-PROB-p0015-s10] Then there exists a circle packing of T with carrier D.
    [MATH-PROB-p0015-s12] Indeed, it implies that the circle packing of a CP hyperbolic triangulation is not determined up to Möbius transformations and reflections, since, for example, we can circle pack the same triangulation in both the unit disc and the unit square, and these two packings are clearly not related by a Möbius transformation.
- MATH-PROB-C08-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: For an infinite simple plane triangulation, the statements that a transient triangulation has a circle packing with carrier $\mathbb{U}$ and that a circle packing with carrier $\mathbb{R}^2$ implies recurrence require the bounded degree assumption, whereas the statements that a recurrent triangulation has a circle packing with carrier $\mathbb{R}^2$ and that a circle packing with carrier $\mathbb{U}$ implies transience are proved without it.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-PROB-p0060-s12] 1. If G is recurrent, then there exists a circle packing P of G such that Carrier(P) = R2. 2.
    [MATH-PROB-p0060-s13] If G is transient, then there exists a circle packing P of G such that Carrier(P) = U.
    [MATH-PROB-p0061-s01] 3. If P is a circle packing of G with Carrier(P) = R2, then G is recurrent. 4.
    [MATH-PROB-p0061-s02] If P is a circle packing of G with Carrier(P) = U, then G is transient.
    [MATH-PROB-p0061-s09] Furthermore, in [40] Theorem 4.4 (1) and Theorem 4.4 (4) are proved without the bounded degrees assumption, but the other two statements require this assumption.
- MATH-PROB-C08-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: Take a triangular lattice circle packing and an infinite horizontal path of circles $C_0, C_1, C_2, \dots$ in it, and in the upper face shared by $C_n$ and $C_{n+1}$ draw $2^n$ circles forming a vertical path, each tangent to both $C_n$ and $C_{n+1}$, with the last of them also tangent to the upper neighbor of $C_n$ and $C_{n+1}$; the resulting plane triangulation has unbounded degrees and a circle packing with carrier $\mathbb{R}^2$, yet its tangency graph is transient.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-PROB-p0061-s10] The following example demonstrates why the bounded degree condition is necessary for Theorem 4.4 (2) and Theorem 4.4 (3).
    [MATH-PROB-p0061-s11] Example 4.8 Let P be a triangular lattice circle packing (as in Fig. 4.3), and let C0, C1, C2, . . . be an infinite horizontal path of circles in P going (say) to the right.
    [MATH-PROB-p0061-s12] In the upper face shared by Cn and Cn+1, draw 2n circles which form a vertical path and each of them tangent both to Cn and Cn+1; the last circle of these is also tangent to the upper neighbor of Cn and Cn+1.
    [MATH-PROB-p0061-s13] See Fig. 4.3. The resulting graph is a plane triangulation and the carrier of the packing is R2.
    [MATH-PROB-p0061-s14] However, it is an easy exercise to verify that the tangency graph of this circle packing is transient.
- MATH-PROB-C08-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: The statement that a plane triangulation can be circle packed in $\mathbb{R}^2$ or in $\mathbb{U}$, but not both, holds without the assumption of bounded degree.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-PROB-p0061-s06] Corollary 4.6 Any bounded degree plane triangulation can be circle-packed in R2
    [MATH-PROB-p0061-s07] or U, but not both.
    [MATH-PROB-p0061-s08] Remark 4.7 In fact, it is proved in [40] that the corollary above holds without the assumption of bounded degree.
- MATH-PROB-C08-S3-04 | S3
  ATOM: The circle packing of a CP hyperbolic triangulation is not determined up to Möbius transformations and reflections in general, because the same triangulation can be circle packed in both the unit disc and the unit square, and these two packings are not related by a Möbius transformation.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-PROB-p0015-s12] Indeed, it implies that the circle packing of a CP hyperbolic triangulation is not determined up to Möbius transformations and reflections, since, for example, we can circle pack the same triangulation in both the unit disc and the unit square, and these two packings are clearly not related by a Möbius transformation.
